records.title: LLM Top 10 2026
records.description: A 122-page reference guide that ranks the ten main security risks of LLM applications for 2026: prompt injection, sensitive information disclosure, excessive agency, supply chain, data and model poisoning, unbounded consumption, misinformation, hidden context exposure, vector and embedding weaknesses, and improper output handling. Each entry gives attack scenarios and mitigations, and the appendices map the risks to ATLAS, the Agentic Top 10, NIST and CWE, and describe an LLM application architecture for threat modelling. It is reading only; there are no exercises.

records.title: Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026
records.description: A peer-reviewed reference guide to the ten main risks of agentic applications (ASI01-ASI10): goal hijack, tool misuse, identity and privilege abuse, agentic supply chain, unexpected code execution, memory and context poisoning, insecure inter-agent communication, cascading failures, human-agent trust exploitation, and rogue agents. Each entry has attack scenarios and mitigations. The appendices map the risks to the LLM Top 10, CycloneDX/AIBOM and the Non-Human Identities Top 10, and include an incident tracker. It is reading only.

records.title: ATLAS (v2026.08)
records.description: A knowledge base of adversary tactics, techniques, mitigations and case studies against AI systems (16 tactics and 84 techniques as of v5.1, Nov 2025). Releases from Dec 2025 to Sep 2026 add many agent techniques: AI agent tool poisoning, supply-chain rug pull, local AI agent compromise, agent configuration discovery, escape to host and deepfake-assisted phishing. New case studies include poisoned MCP servers, EchoLeak and computer-use agent hijacking. It is a reference, not a course; the website is JavaScript-rendered, so content was checked through the release notes.
